For example, if the Rams face the Bengals, and oddsmakers set the spread at Rams -3.5, you would need Los Angeles to win by 4 or more points in order to cash your Rams bet. What is an Over/Under Bet? Over/Under is a wager based on how many points you think will be scored in a specific game. Oddsmakers set the total, and bettors decide whether the final score will be higher or lower than that number. If an Over/Under is set at 44.5 points and you bet Over, you will need the combined score of both teams to be 45 points or higher to win your bet. What is a Moneyline Bet? A moneyline bet involves choosing which team you believe will win a specific matchup. The moneyline favorite carries a minus designation, like -130. This means that you need to wager $130 to earn a $100 profit. Conversely, the underdog carries a plus designation, like +110. This means that you win $110 in profit on a $100 bet. Our NFL Player Prop Bet Cheat Sheet assists bettors by comparing lines from leading sportsbooks with our daily NFL projections. What is an NFL player prop bet? An NFL player prop bet is a type of wager where you’re betting on the performance of a specific player in a game rather than the overall outcome. For example, you might place a bet on how many passing yards a quarterback will throw for, or how many touchdowns a running back will score. It’s a fun way to get more invested in the action, especially if you’re confident in how a particular player will perform, regardless of who wins or loses the game. It’s like focusing on one slice of the pie instead of the whole thing. Whether you're new to sports betting or a betting pro, our Sports Betting Strategy and Advice page is for you.

results.title: 2026 NFL Week 11 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Bucs Are Live As Touchdown Underdogs
results.description: Geoff Schwartz likes Tampa Bay to keep it close in Detroit and has a Christian McCaffrey prop for Vikings-49ers in Mexico City.
highlights: 2026 NFL Week 11 Best Bets, Expert Picks: Bucs Are Live As Touchdown Underdogs Kirk Cousins was the story of Week 10. Now the Vikings get their biggest test yet. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports. The Vikings are a different team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game.

The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week.

The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover.

NFL Player Prop Pick #1: Christian McCaffrey Rushing Yards Christian McCaffrey’s rushing yards have stayed under 74.5 in eight of nine games. His median is 64 yards. Even his best game, a 75-yard afternoon against Arizona, would have beaten my projected line by just half a yard. McCaffrey has had seven, 18 and 13 carries in his last three games. Las Vegas was the one opponent in that stretch against whom he got a steady afternoon of handoffs. He finished with 68 yards. Dallas gave up 161 receiving yards to McCaffrey on just four catches.

Early NFL Player Props for Week 11: James Cook, Christian McCaffrey & More My early Week 11 NFL player props start with two running backs coming off very different Sundays James Cook broke a 74-yard run for Buffalo, while Christian McCaffrey did most of his damage as a receiver See my three Week 11 NFL prop picks and projected lines below James Cook ran for 157 yards against the Jets. Christian McCaffrey had 161 yards receiving against Dallas. Both performances will draw attention to their Week 11 NFL player props, but I’d approach their rushing totals very differently. Here are the three NFL player props I’m targeting and the opening numbers I’d play.

I want his rushing under if the line opens in the mid-70s: he can hurt Minnesota on a screen or a wheel route without adding a yard to his rushing total. Minnesota has allowed 4.2 yards per carry on 241 attempts. The workload I’d worry about is 18 or 19 carries. In the mid-70s, I’m happy to let his receiving yards grab the headlines. results.title: NFL Week 3 betting guide: Analysis and top plays for Sunday's games
results.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 3 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
highlights: Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites).

The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career.

If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.
